entities.name: Abul-Fazl Bayhaqi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abūʾl-Fazl Muḥammad ibn Ḥusayn Bayhaqī, better known as Abu'l-Fazl Bayhaqi, was a secretary, historian and author who lived from approximately 1017 to 1077 CE. He was born in the city of Balkh, in present-day Afghanistan, and served as a scribe and translator in the court of the Seljuk Sultan, Malikshah I. Bayhaqi's most famous work is the 'Tajziyat-i Tawhid' (The Illumination of Unity), a comprehensive history of Islam from its origins to the 11th century CE.

Bayhaqi's historical significance lies in his ability to bridge the cultural and linguistic divide between Persian and Arabic, making his works accessible to a wider audience. His contributions to the field of Islamic history and his role in preserving ancient texts have made him a significant figure in the annals of Islamic scholarship.

In the 12th century CE, Bayhaqi's works were translated into Latin by scholars in the court of the Holy Roman Emperor, Frederick I, further spreading the knowledge of Islamic history and culture.

Today, Bayhaqi's 'Tajziyat-i Tawhid' remains a seminal work in the field of Islamic history, providing valuable insights into the evolution of Islamic thought and culture during the medieval period.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, Bayhaqi's name continues to be invoked in academic circles, and his works continue to inspire scholars and researchers seeking to understand the complexities of Islamic history and culture.
